In [[operator algebras]], the '''Toeplitz algebra''' is the [[C*-algebra]] generated by the [[unilateral shift]] on the [[Hilbert space]] [[sequence space|''l''<sup>2</sup>('''N''')]].<ref>{{citation|title=A Short Course in Spectral Theory|volume=209|series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics|first=Arveson|last=William|date=9 November 2001 |publisher=Springer|isbn=0387953000}}</ref> Identifying ''l''<sup>2</sup>('''N''') with the [[Hardy space]] [[H square|''H''<sup>2</sup>]], the Toeplitz algebra consists of elements of the form

:<math>T_f + K\;</math>

where ''<math>T_f</math>'' is a [[Toeplitz operator]] with continuous symbol <math display="inline">f</math> and ''K'' is a [[compact operator on Hilbert space|compact operator]]. 

Toeplitz operators with continuous symbols commute modulo the compact operators. So the Toeplitz algebra can be viewed as the C*-algebra extension of continuous functions on the circle by the compact operators. This extension is called the '''Toeplitz extension'''. 

By [[Atkinson's theorem]], an element of the Toeplitz algebra ''<math display="inline">T_f + K\;</math>''is a [[Fredholm operator]] if and only if the symbol <math display="inline">f</math> of ''<math>T_f</math>'' is invertible. In that case, the Fredholm index of ''<math>T_f + K\;</math>''is precisely the [[winding number]] of ''f'', the equivalence class of ''f'' in the [[fundamental group]] of the circle. This is a special case of the [[Atiyah-Singer index theorem]].

[[Wold decomposition]] characterizes [[isometry|proper isometries]] acting on a Hilbert space. From this, together with properties of Toeplitz operators, one can conclude that the Toeplitz algebra is the [[universal C*-algebra]] generated by a proper isometry; this is ''Coburn's theorem''<ref>Coburn, Lewis A. "The C^*-algebra generated by an isometry." (1967): 722-726.</ref>.
